cities.name: London
cities.why: Global finance. Old wealth. Sovereign capital.

6.note: Ascot, Wimbledon, Chelsea Flower Show. Mayfair at its densest.

7.note: Wimbledon closes. The exodus to the Mediterranean begins.

10.note: Frieze and auction season. Hedge funds return from the coast.

cities.name: New York
cities.why: Markets. Hedge funds. Media. Auctions.

5.note: Spring marquee sales. Dinner tables set around the salerooms.

9.note: Return week. Everyone is back and pretending they never left.

11.note: Autumn auctions. The largest private dinners of the American year.

cities.name: Miami
cities.why: American family-office winter headquarters.

1.note: Winter headquarters fully staffed. Northeast capital has landed.

2.note: Season peak. Brickell and the Design District run parallel.

3.note: Still warm. The Palm Beach overflow sits here.

5.note: The paddock arrives. Hardrock Stadium is background noise.

12.note: Art Basel week. Miami becomes America's capital for six days.

cities.name: Monaco
cities.why: The European wealth operating system.

5.note: The race is background noise. The terraces above Turn One are not.

6.note: Fleet forming. Tenders running to Antibes and back.

7.note: Transit hub for the Sardinian and Balearic legs.

8.note: Half the harbour is elsewhere. The offices are not.

9.note: Yacht Show. Not a boat show. A liquidity event with three days of runway.

cities.name: Dubai
cities.why: Gulf capital. Crypto. Sovereign money.

1.note: Peak season. Family offices operating at full weight.

2.note: Conference density high. The margins matter more than the stages.

3.note: Season closing. Capital rotates toward Europe.

12.note: Sovereign capital active through the F1 close in Abu Dhabi.

cities.name: Singapore
cities.why: Asian family offices.

9.note: Night race weekend. The only week the city's family offices are fully visible.

10.note: Post-race. Deals started at the paddock get paperwork.

cities.name: Hong Kong
cities.why: China gateway.

3.note: Art Basel Hong Kong. Asian collectors and the dealers who follow them.

5.note: Spring sales. Auction houses run the calendar.

cities.name: Geneva
cities.why: Banking. Commodities. Diplomacy.

5.note: Watch sales. The quietest high-value week in Europe.

11.note: Autumn sales. Geneva is loud for four days a year and this is two of them.

cities.name: Zurich
cities.why: Asset preservation.

venues.name: The Restaurant at The Dolder Grand

1.note: Davos staging. Every arrival lands here first.

cities.name: Paris
cities.why: Luxury. Fashion. The LVMH ecosystem.

1.note: Couture. The smallest rooms of the fashion year.

3.note: Ready-to-wear. The maisons run the city for nine days.

9.note: Ready-to-wear returns. Dinner tables are harder than the shows.

10.note: Paris+ par Art Basel. The collector base moves from London to here in 72 hours.

cities.name: St. Barths
cities.why: The Caribbean transition. Where the year is decided before it starts.

1.note: Nobody discusses work. Everyone discusses who is buying what.

2.note: Emptying. The fleet turns toward the Atlantic crossing.

12.note: Arrivals begin the 26th. The harbour fills in four days.

cities.name: St. Moritz
cities.why: European aristocracy, Swiss banking, German industrial families.

1.note: The transition week. Snow polo and the lounges behind it.

2.note: White Turf. The oldest guest list in the Alps.

12.note: Season opening. Families arrive before the fireworks.

cities.name: Davos
cities.why: Public: the Forum. Private: every hotel lobby and suite in the valley.

cities.name: Aspen
cities.why: American capital migrates. Snow replaces yachts.

1.note: New Year density holds through the second week.

2.note: Peak. The Caribou list is the actual guest list.

12.note: Holiday weeks. Booked eighteen months out.

cities.name: Palm Beach
cities.why: Not an event. An operating system.

venues.name: The Society of the Four Arts

1.note: Season underway. Old industrial wealth and the political donor class.

2.note: Full weight. The most underreported concentration in America.

3.note: Peak. Nobody puts this on a wealth calendar. That is the point.

11.note: Season reopening ahead of the holidays.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.why: Not loud. Very high quality.

4.note: Cherry blossom season quietly pulls Asian finance and luxury retail.

10.note: Autumn. Collector traffic without the crowd.

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.why: The satellite dinners matter more than the panels.

2.note: Frieze LA. The West Coast collector base makes itself visible for one week.

5.note: Milken week. Every private dinner within five miles goes invitation-only.

cities.name: Cannes
cities.why: The red carpet matters least. The yachts matter most.

5.note: Two weeks. The anchorage is the actual venue.

cities.name: Sun Valley
cities.why: Probably the highest concentration of billionaire decision-makers on Earth.

7.note: Everything else pauses. Nobody publishes the guest list. The airport does.

8.note: Residual. Families stay on after the conference clears.

cities.name: Porto Cervo
cities.why: The Mediterranean capital. Not Italy. Not Sardinia. The marina.

6.note: Fleet arriving. The season has not started.

7.note: Full weight. Helicopter arrivals run continuously.

8.note: Ferragosto. The densest two weeks in the Mediterranean.

9.note: Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup, then the Swan Cup. The marina holds its weight into the second week, then empties toward Monaco.

cities.name: Pebble Beach
cities.why: Collectors. Industrialists. Automotive dynasties.

8.note: Car Week. Three days that price an entire asset class.

cities.name: The Hamptons
cities.why: New York, relocated, with worse traffic and better lawns.

6.note: Season opens Memorial Day. The city thins.

7.note: Full weight. Benefit season runs the calendar.

8.note: Peak. Every Friday helicopter slot is spoken for.

9.note: Labor Day closes it. The best two weeks are after.

cities.name: Mykonos
cities.why: The loudest room on the Mediterranean circuit.

8.note: Peak. The beach clubs price like they know it.

cities.name: Ibiza
cities.why: The Balearic leg. Quieter money than the reputation suggests.

6.note: Season opening. The fleet arrives ahead of the crowd.

8.note: Peak. The north of the island is where the actual weight sits.

9.note: Closing parties. Better rooms, fewer people.

cities.name: Capri
cities.why: Small island, old money, no room to hide.

7.note: Anchorage filling. The Amalfi leg begins.

8.note: Peak. Tender traffic is the reliable indicator.

cities.name: Lake Como
cities.why: Where the Mediterranean circuit goes to be quiet.

5.note: Concorso d'Eleganza. Collectors before the coast fills.

8.note: Peak. Villa bookings run three years deep.

9.note: Closing. The best light of the year.

cities.name: Gstaad
cities.why: The most closed guest list in the Alps.

1.note: New Year residency. Chalets held in families for generations.

12.note: Holiday weeks. Entry is inherited, not booked.

cities.name: Jackson Hole
cities.why: Two different crowds, one valley.

8.note: Central banking symposium. The valley's other guest list.

cities.name: Nantucket
cities.why: Old American wealth, deliberately understated.

7.note: Season peak. Ferry and airfield traffic tell the story.

cities.name: Abu Dhabi
cities.why: Formula 1 closes. Sovereign capital opens.

11.note: Building. Sovereign funds set the year's posture.

12.note: Season finale. The hospitality suites are the actual event.

cities.name: Venice
cities.why: Biennale years only. Then it is the densest collector week in Europe.

4.note: Biennale preview week. Palazzo dinners run the schedule.

9.note: The Lido. Eleven days in which the people buying and the people selling cannot avoid each other.

cities.name: Basel
cities.why: The art market's actual centre of gravity.

6.note: First-choice day is the market. Everything after is retail.

cities.name: Maastricht
cities.why: Old masters, jewellery, and the quietest serious money in art.

3.note: TEFAF. Museum acquisition budgets meet private collections.

cities.name: Milan
cities.why: Fashion, design, and the industrial families behind both.

2.note: Fashion week. The showroom appointments matter more than the runways.

4.note: Salone del Mobile. The city's highest-density week, full stop.

cities.name: Courchevel
cities.why: The altiport is the guest list.

1.note: Orthodox Christmas through mid-January. A distinct arrival pattern.

cities.name: Austin
cities.why: The American paddock stop that turned into a capital week.

10.note: Race week. Tech capital and the F1 hospitality overlay.

cities.name: Las Vegas
cities.why: The newest stop and the most heavily brokered.

11.note: Night race. Suites priced as a distinct asset class.

cities.name: Monza
cities.why: The oldest room on the paddock circuit.

9.note: Italian Grand Prix. Como absorbs the overflow.

cities.name: Silverstone
cities.why: The British leg. London empties into it for four days.

7.note: British Grand Prix. Mayfair relocates north.

cities.name: Melbourne
cities.why: Where the paddock year opens.

3.note: Season opener. The year's hospitality posture is set here.
